documents.title: Phylogenomics, spatiotemporal transcriptional dynamics and Cis-regulatory architecture underlying the Portulaca oleracea antioxidant network under extreme salinity.
documents.abstract: Global soil salinization severely threatens agricultural productivity. Portulaca oleracea L., an extreme xerohalophyte, displays exceptional salinity tolerance, yet the transcriptional architecture coordinating its antioxidant defenses across organs and developmental stages remains unresolved. In this study, multi-tissue high-throughput RNA-Seq, quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) validation, comparative phylogenomics across 154 plant genomes, and condition-specific gene regulatory network (GRN) modeling were integrated to characterize 436 antioxidant loci in P. oleracea. documents.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

documents.title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
documents.abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysoz

documents.title: An integrative systems biology framework decodes peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures, systemic interactome networks, and candidate targets in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
documents.abstract: To characterize systemic transcriptomic signatures and identify candidate hub genes associated with lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) in peripheral blood using an integrative systems-biology approach.

documents.title: Beyond the Primary-Secondary Dichotomy: Toward a Unified Metabolic Perspective.
documents.abstract: The distinction between primary and secondary metabolism has long provided a useful conceptual and pedagogical framework in biochemistry, particularly in plant sciences, but it increasingly fails as a literal description of how metabolites are produced and function. Pathways share precursors, cofactors, regulatory mechanisms, transport systems, and recycling routes, while metabolites conventionally assigned to different categories can contribute to growth, signaling, defense, nutrient acquisition, structure, or stress responses depending on context. documents.title: The Maladaptive Stress State: A Systems Framework for Chronic Disease Persistence.
documents.abstract: Chronic degenerative diseases are traditionally explained in terms of disease-specific initiating lesions and molecular pathways. Although this approach has substantially advanced understanding of disease mechanisms, it does not fully explain why biologically diverse disorders often converge on persistent states marked by chronic inflammation, impaired repair, altered nutrient sensing, reduced adaptive flexibility, and incomplete recovery after the initiating insult subsides. This Perspective proposes the Maladaptive Stress State (MSS), a systems-level framework that distinguishes disease init

documents.title: Meta-finetuning foundation models for generalizable biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes.
documents.abstract: Biological image segmentation is essential for analyzing cellular structures, yet labeled data are often labor-intensive and expensive to obtain, which limits conventional deep learning models in low-data settings. Building upon the bi-level meta-finetuning formulation introduced in BLO-SAM, we evaluate MetaTune for adapting foundation models to biological image segmentation in ultra-low-data regimes. MetaTune separates the model's learnable components into meta-parameters, which enhance generalization, and non-meta parameters, which focus on task-specific adaptation. Through an iterative, two

documents.title: Causal assessment of Bayesian gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference is an essential tool for revealing dysregulated relationships between genes in different cell types from single-cell transcriptomic (SCT) data. GRNs based on Bayesian networks (BNs) learned from SCT data can elucidate directed regulatory relationships representing complex disease mechanisms and their interplay through graphical modeling. However, software for learning BNs from SCT data is not widely available, nor is software for evaluating the BNs' structural accuracy in representing causal relationships between genes. Here, we describe the scstruc R pa

documents.title: Bridging traditional knowledge and modern technology: In-silico ethnopharmacology in herbal drug discovery.
documents.abstract: The use of herbal medicines and phytochemicals has gained considerable attention due to their structural diversity, selective toxicity, lower incidence of adverse effects, and affordability compared to conventional chemotherapy. Nevertheless, their precise mechanisms of action and bioactive constituents remain insufficiently understood, limiting their clinical translation and highlighting the need for rigorous scientific investigation. This review provides an integrative perspective on herbal-based drug discovery, beginning with the intersection of traditional disease classification systems, s
documents.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

documents.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
documents.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C

documents.title: Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference.
documents.abstract: Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information.

documents.title: Dolphin semen metabolome characterization and relationships with sperm quality.
documents.abstract: Identification and quantification of metabolites in semen can augment assisted reproductive technologies by indicating reproductive health and fertility. Species-specific semen metabolites associated with improved semen quality remain largely unknown in exotic species due to limited sample availability.
documents.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society

documents.title: A single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas reveals the endodermal gene regulatory network underlying Arabidopsis stem gravitropism.
documents.abstract: Gravitropism redirects plant organ growth by converting gravity perception into asymmetric growth initiated in endodermal statocytes. Although the C2H2-type zinc finger transcription factor SHOOT GRAVITROPISM 5 (SGR5), also known as INDETERMINATE DOMAIN 15 (IDD15), is essential for shoot gravitropism, the transcriptional mechanisms linking gravity perception to directional growth remain unclear.

documents.title: Longevitomics as the science of the longevitome: Towards a unified systems science of healthy longevity.
documents.abstract: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of

documents.title: Host-like temperature unlocks glucose uptake and metabolism in pathogenic Leptospira.
documents.abstract: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions. Although Leptospira is generally considered to rely primarily on long-chain fatty acids for growth and to have limited capacity to use glucose, whether host-like temperature alters glucose-associated metabolic capacity remains unclear. Here, we used transcriptome-integrated genome-scale metabolic modeling to examine temperature-dependent metabolic states in pathogenic Leptospira. documents.title: Network inference at single-cell resolution reveals morphoregulatory divergence and multilayered buffering in limb evolution.
documents.abstract: How changes in conserved developmental genetic programs contribute to morphological evolution remains poorly understood, particularly in non-conventional model species. Here, we combine single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin-accessibility profiling with cross-species label transfer and gene regulatory network inference to compare mouse and pig limb development. Our analyses identify broadly conserved cellular organization but discrete divergence in HOX-, FGF- and SHH-regulated programs. documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Engineering rhizosphere microbial consortia for soil bioremediation: Mechanisms, field constraints, and evidence-based design.
documents.abstract: Soil contamination continues to threaten ecosystem health and agricultural productivity worldwide. However, rhizosphere-mediated bioremediation has emerged as a nature-inspired, sustainable approach for mitigating these impacts. This review advocates field-scale implementation of rhizosphere microbiome engineering by exploiting interactions among plants, microorganisms, and soil. Unlike previous reviews that primarily summarize rhizosphere-mediated remediation processes, it integrates mechanistic, ecological, and engineering perspectives to identify critical barriers limiting field performance
documents.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

documents.title: scPhyloGRN: gene regulatory network inference guided by lineage topology in single-cell developmental data.
documents.abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference from single-cell transcriptomes is complicated by expression patterns associated with both cell state and shared ancestry. Cellular phylogenies provide developmental context, but incorporating relationships among individual cells into gene-level regulatory inference remains challenging.

documents.title: A time-resolved single-nucleus atlas of cochlear aging reveals biphasic inflammaging and Tbx2-dependent inner hair cell maintenance.
documents.abstract: Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is the most prevalent sensory deficit in older adults, yet its molecular progression remains poorly resolved. Few cochlear single-cell studies have integrated cell-cell communication, gene regulatory network (GRN) reconstruction, and cross-cohort bulk validation into one temporal framework.

documents.title: Protamine gene expression is associated with sperm motility in rams: An integrative experimental and gene network analysis.
documents.abstract: Protamine 1 (PRM1) and protamine 2 (PRM2) are essential regulators of sperm chromatin condensation and genome integrity, and their dysregulation has been associated with impaired male fertility. However, their role in rams remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigated the relationship between protamine gene expression and semen quality in rams and explored their potential upstream regulatory mechanisms using gene regulatory network (GRN) analysis. Fifteen ejaculates from five rams were analyzed. Based on total sperm motility using computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), ejacul

documents.title: Comparative phylogenomics and transcriptional regulatory networks of AQPs, HSPs, and LEA proteins in salt-stressed Portulaca oleracea.
documents.abstract: Soil salinization severely threatens global food security, necessitating systematic investigations of halophytes like Portulaca oleracea to decode the molecular mechanisms of environmental resilience. Utilizing an integrated framework of deep learning-based genome annotation (58,817 predicted genes; 96.5% BUSCO completeness), multi-tissue RNA-Seq, phylogenomics, and gene regulatory network (GRN) inference, the synergistic orchestration of 78 aquaporins (AQPs), 525 heat shock proteins (HSPs), and 119 late embryogenesis abundant (LEA) proteins was elucidated. documents.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology

documents.title: Decoding the epithelial-stromal interactome in allergic rhinitis through single-cell multiomics integration.
documents.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a prevalent chronic condition, yet the cellular and molecular changes associated with its pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
documents.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

documents.title: A pathogen-free citrus model recapitulates Huanglongbing-associated molecular and physiological reprogramming.
documents.abstract: Huanglongbing (HLB) is a devastating citrus disease associated with "Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus", but the contribution of host-driven processes to disease development remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a pathogen-free system to determine whether chloroplast dysfunction can reproduce key molecular and physiological features of HLB. Using Citrus tristeza virus-mediated silencing of phytoene desaturase (PDS) and δ-aminolevulinic acid dehydratase (ALAD), we simultaneously disrupted carotenoid and chlorophyll biosynthesis in Citrus macrophylla. documents.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology

documents.title: Multi-omic analysis reveals maturation programs in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes during long-term culture.
documents.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold tremendous promise for disease modeling, drug discovery, and cardiac regenerative therapies. However, the immature phenotype of hPSC-CMs remains a major barrier limiting their translational utility. Here, we performed integrated multi-omic profiling to identify molecular pathways and regulatory programs associated with hPSC-CM maturation during long-term culture. hPSC-CMs were cultured for 113 days and analyzed using metabolomics, proteomics, and transcriptomics across progressive stages of maturation. documents.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

documents.title: TREM2 signaling in cardiovascular disease: macrophage heterogeneity, timing, and therapeutic opportunity.
documents.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with pathogenesis extending beyond hemodynamic derangements to involve chronic, maladaptive immune-metabolic crosstalk. Macrophage functional identity has evolved beyond the M1/M2 paradigm toward a model of high heterogeneity and dynamic plasticity, wherein Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) serves as a pivotal molecular hub.

documents.title: Causality analysis of toxicological mechanisms in networked systems such as adverse outcome pathway networks.
documents.abstract: This paper examines why robust causality assessment is central to toxicology yet increasingly difficult in networked biological systems, including Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) networks and multi-omics datasets. Classical causal frameworks (e.g., Koch/Dale reasoning and Bradford Hill-type considerations) remain useful for scoping, but they offer limited operational guidance for multifactorial, nonlinear, and feedback-dominated mechanisms. documents.title: Systems Biology and Machine Learning Reveal Oxidative Stress Hubs and Therapeutic Targets in Diarrhea-Predominant Irritable Bowel Syndrome.
documents.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a common functional gastrointestinal disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that oxidative stress is involved in its pathophysiology. This study explored oxidative stress-related mechanisms in IBS-D and screened potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrative bioinformatics analysis.

documents.title: BoolFunc-EA: A Boolean-evolutionary approach for accurate inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series gene expression data.
documents.abstract: Network inference is the process of discovering genetic information from time-series data. The inference of gene regulatory networks from time-series data represents a significant challenge in bioinformatics. Despite the development of many Boolean network inference methods, most struggle with scalability as they impose restrictions on regulatory genes for each target gene. Other methods suffer from local optimum issues or are unable to compute the exact mutual information between a regulatory gene and its target gene. To resolve these issues, we present a novel method referred to as BoolFunc-

documents.title: The ovarian cellular ecosystem in polycystic ovary syndrome: from cellular heterogeneity to clinical relevance.
documents.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most biologically heterogeneous disorders in reproductive endocrinology, extending far beyond the classical features of hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, and polycystic ovarian morphology. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the endocrine, metabolic, genetic, epigenetic, and inflammatory mechanisms associated with PCOS, these processes have largely been investigated independently, and their contribution to the marked clinical and biological heterogeneity of the disorder remains incompletely understood. documents.title: ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models.
documents.abstract: Air pollution is one of the leading global environmental health risks, associated with millions of premature deaths annually. It represents a substantial share of the global disease burden. Despite well-established epidemiological associations, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain only partially understood. There is a need for systematic approaches toward mechanistic understanding that connect particulate matter exposure to downstream pathways and pathophysiological effects.
